newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe air force to buy eight new aircraft. [CORRECTED 13:47 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe air force to buy eight new aircraft. [CORRECTED 13:47 GMT]

text.p: Zimbabwe plans to buy four Hawk fighter jets from Britain and four helicopters from a French-German company to replenish an ageing air force fleet, Defence Minister Moven Mahachi was quoted on Friday as saying.
Mahachi declined to give the cost of the aircraft in an interview published in The Zimbabwe Independent. Some defence experts put the cost at around one billion Zimbabwe dollars ($88 million).

The Hawk fighter jets, produced by British Aerospace, and the Agusta (corrects from Agouster) Bell helicopters from Eurocopter -- a merger of the helicopter divisions of France's Aerospatiale and Germany's Daimler-Benz -- would be acquired in the coming months, Mahachi said.
He added the Zimbabwe Defence Force was not increasing its fleet but simply replacing old assets.

Defence spending has accounted for over 25 percent of Zimbabwe's annual budgets over the last 17 years, making it one of the biggest contributors to a budget deficit that has averaged 10 percent of annual gross domestic product over the same period.
